findings.title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed at repository root
findings.body: A git submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` was added at the root of the repository without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will cause `git submodule` commands and tooling that inspects the tree to fail or behave unexpectedly, and should be removed before merging.

findings.title: Cache key uses non-deterministic `hash()` and redundant cache layer breaks tests and cross-worker invalidation
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` build a shared cache key using Python's built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Because `PYTHONHASHSEED` randomizes `hash()` across processes (and even for tuple of ints, `hash()` is not a stable cache key primitive across Python versions/architectures and can collide), `invalidate_upsampling_cache` called from one worker is not guaranteed to match keys written by another. In addition, `sentry.options.get` already caches option values in memory and in `default_store.cache`, so this extra 60-second cache in `django.core.cache` is redundant and causes stale results in tests (and production) whenever the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes within 60 seconds for the same `(org_id, project_ids)` pair—which is actually happens in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` if the cache is not flushed between test methods.

findings.title: Upsampling check passes outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` and ignores `query` parameter
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` rather than `scoped_dataset`, and `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET.get("query")` instead of the `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`. When dashboard widget splitting runs in `get_event_stats_factory`, `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset=discover` and modified queries such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"` while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` (or `metrics_performance`). Because `dataset` is not `discover` or `errors`, upsampling will never be applied to split error widget queries, or if `request.GET["query"]` contained `event.type:error`, it would also be evaluated against the wrong query string when checking transaction-only splits.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` does not handle NULL/0 `sample_weight` and should be marked `private=True`
findings.body: In `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter`, `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with `default_result_type="number"` and without `private=True`. For events in allowlisted projects that were ingested before client error sampling was enabled or from SDKs that did not set `sample_weight`, `sample_weight` can be `NULL` or `0` (unlike `ifNull(nullIf(sample_weight, 0), 1)`), causing those events to contribute `0` to the sum instead of `1` and undercounting real errors. Furthermore, because `private=True` is omitted, `upsampled_count()` is exposed as a public Discover query function to all users and organizations, and its `default_result_type` is `"number"` instead of `"integer"` (unlike `count()`, which returns `"integer"`).
